title: Social Services Legislation Amendment (Family Assistance Alignment and Other Measures) Bill 2016
short_title: Social Services Legislation Amendment (Family Assistance Alignment and Other Measures) Bill 2016

summary.attribution: Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
sentences: This bill would set clear rules for when new or increased family tax benefit payments take effect after certain review decisions.
It would amend the Family Assistance Administration Act to specify date of effect rules for top-up payments and supplements.
The bill also includes contingent amendments to remove or change these measures if another bill phasing out FTB supplements by 1 July 2018 becomes law.
changes: Introduces date of effect rules for review decisions that create new or increased family tax benefit entitlements.
Proposes contingent amendments to repeal or revise the measures if the Structural Reform Bill is enacted.
Addresses an unintended consequence of previous amendments to the Youth Allowance Rate Calculator.
summary.affected: Families receiving family tax benefit and youth allowance recipients.

speeches.speaker: Jenny Macklin
speeches.brief: Labor supported the Social Services Legislation Amendment (Family Assistance Alignment and Other Measures) Bill 2016 as technical, but opposed further cuts to family tax benefit end-of-year supplements. The speaker also accused Minister for Social Services of using misleading figures, citing ACOSS, Greg Jericho, Ross Gittins, and Cassandra Goldie, and referenced $8.5 billion in previous Liberal cuts and $2 billion in proposed cuts.

speeches.speaker: Dan Tehan
speeches.brief: The bill reinforces the one-year time frame for family tax benefit income reconciliation for 2012–13 to 2014–15, clarifies arrears payment rules, and corrects a youth allowance rate calculator error to produce fortnightly amounts. The opposition supported the technical amendments but opposed further cuts to the family tax benefit supplement.
